blocks.content: Course: API Handling with Asynchronous Javascript
A Promise tracks the status of an async task over time.
It can be in only one state at a time, and it moves in one direction only.
Every promise is always in one of three states:

rows: The task has started but the result is not yet ready.
The task completed successfully and the result is ready. So the promise is done.
An error occurred and the task failed. So the promise is done (failure also counts as the promise being "done".

blocks.content: A promise starts out in the pending state, and either moves to the fulfilled or rejected state, but not both.
Once fulfilled or rejected, the Promise never changes again.
